suit.definition: A set of garments (usually including a jacket and trousers or skirt) for outerwear all of the same fabric and color.

dress-shirt.definition: A smart collared shirt worn with formal or business clothing.

tie.definition: Neckwear consisting of a long narrow piece of material worn (mostly by men) under a collar and tied in knot at the front.

bow-tie.definition: A man's necktie is designed to form two loops like a bow.

cufflinks.definition: Jewelry consisting of one of a pair of linked buttons used to fasten the cuffs of a shirt.

pocket-square.definition: A small decorative piece of fabric folded and placed in the breast pocket of a jacket.
pocket-square.exampleUsage: The suit included a plain pocket square.

suspenders.definition: Elastic straps that hold trousers up.

vest.definition: A man's sleeveless garment worn underneath a coat.

dress-pants.definition: Trousers designed for formal or smart clothing rather than casual or athletic wear.
dress-pants.exampleUsage: He wore dress pants with a jacket.

evening-gown.definition: A formal dress, usually reaching the floor, worn by women at evening events such as balls, galas, or formal dinners.

cocktail-dress.definition: A smart dress worn for semi-formal social events.
cocktail-dress.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Cocktail Dress" in an educational description.

pencil-skirt.definition: A straight narrow skirt that follows the line of the body and usually reaches around the knee.
pencil-skirt.exampleUsage: The workwear display included a knee-length pencil skirt.

blazer.definition: A smart jacket worn as part of a suit or with other clothes.

silk-blouse.definition: A blouse made from silk or a silk-like fabric.
silk-blouse.exampleUsage: The formal outfit included a silk blouse.

pantsuit.definition: A pair of pants and a matching jacket worn by women.

wrap-dress.definition: A dress that crosses over the body and fastens with a tie or belt, creating soft, hanging folds.

shawl.definition: Cloak consisting of an oblong piece of cloth used to cover the head and shoulders.

clutch-purse.definition: A small handbag without long handles, designed to be held in the hand or under the arm.
clutch-purse.exampleUsage: She carried a simple clutch purse.

button-down.definition: A shirt with buttons that fasten the points of its collar.

cardigan.definition: A knitted garment that opens at the front and is worn over other clothes.

ankle-pants.definition: Trousers cut to end at or just above the ankle.
ankle-pants.exampleUsage: The ankle pants ended just above the shoes.

flats.definition: Footwear (shoes or slippers) with no heel (or a very low heel).

polo.definition: A shirt with a collar and a short buttoned opening at the neck.

knit-top.definition: A shirt or upper-body garment made from knitted fabric.
knit-top.exampleUsage: The outfit included a lightweight knit top.

oxford-shoes.definition: Formal lace-up shoes with a closed-lacing design.
oxford-shoes.exampleUsage: Polished Oxford shoes completed the formal outfit.

uniform.definition: Standard clothing worn by members of an organization or profession.

scrubs.definition: Loose protective clothing worn by medical workers.

lab-coat.definition: Protective outerwear worn over ordinary clothes in a laboratory helps shield the wearer from spills and contaminating substances.

hard-hat.definition: A rigid protective helmet worn at a work site.

safety-vest.definition: A bright protective garment that makes a worker easy to see.

steel-toe-boots.definition: Boots with protective metal covering over the toes.

coveralls.definition: A loose-fitting protective garment that is worn over other clothing.

gloves.definition: Hand coverings worn for protection while working.

name-tag.definition: A small label showing someone’s name, worn on clothing or a cord so others can identify them.
